newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dubinin sees no radical Russian monetary change.
newsitem.headline: Dubinin sees no radical Russian monetary change.

text.p: Radical changes in Russian monetary and currency policy are unlikely in 1998, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday.

"It's too soon to say exactly what currency policy model will be finally adopted for 1998, but the Central Bank assumes that there will not be any dramatic changes, either in technical management, or in connection with currency and monetary policy," he told a meeting of senior Finance Ministry officials.

The rouble is currently depreciating in a currency band, known as a sloping corridor, which will see the rouble in a 5,730-6,350 per dollar range by the end of the year compared with 5,500-6,100 at the start of the year.
The policy was introduced in mid-1995 and the rouble has never strayed outside the range, or even outside the Central Bank's much narrower bid/offer spread set within the daily corridor.

The Finance Ministry is also pushing down Treasury bill yields, which have reached record low levels, by simply rolling over maturing domestic debt rather than funding the deficit with new borrowing. The successful placement of Russia's first two Eurobonds has enabled the government to shift the emphasis of borrowing to foreign debt.
